name: Clove Bud
source_reference: ISO 3141:1997 - Oil of clove bud; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960; Chaieb et al., Phytotherapy Research, 2007
notes: Clove bud oil has lower eugenol and more esters than clove leaf or stem oils. Clove leaf oil is cheaper but harsher (eugenol 80-95%). Clove stem oil is intermediate.

key_markers.97-53-0: Eugenol - dominant warm, spicy, clove character
key_markers.93-28-7: Eugenyl acetate - sweet, fruity, balsamic ester; quality marker distinguishing bud from leaf oil

olfactive_description: Warm, rich, intensely spicy with a sweet, slightly fruity ester top note. Deep phenolic warmth with a woody-peppery drydown. Full-bodied and tenacious.
